description: A child-directed app may collect a persistent identifier without parental consent only when the identifier supports internal operations. Use of advertising identifiers or cross-app tracking APIs indicates collection that goes beyond internal operations and requires verifiable parental consent.

interpretations.interpretation: Reading an advertising identifier in a child-directed app is collection of a persistent identifier for a purpose other than internal operations and therefore requires prior verifiable parental consent.
The identifier is read only for frequency capping or fraud prevention, which may qualify as support for internal operations.

examples: Delete calls to ASIdentifierManager.shared().advertisingIdentifier and remove NSUserTrackingUsageDescription
Add <uses-permission android:name="com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID" tools:node="remove" /> to the kids flavor manifest
remediation.summary: Remove advertising identifier access and the AD_ID permission from a child-directed build, or gate the code behind a completed verifiable parental consent.

title: Advertising identifiers in a kids app need parental consent

description: Configuration or code that sets retention, expiry, or TTL to forever, never, unlimited, or a disabled value conflicts with the ban on indefinite retention of children's personal information.

interpretations.interpretation: Any explicit setting that disables expiry for stored user data violates the indefinite-retention ban.
The match concerns non-personal data such as a cache or a feature flag and is harmless.

examples: Set Firebase Analytics data retention to a bounded period instead of 'never expire' for user-level data.
remediation.summary: Replace unlimited or disabled retention settings with a finite retention window for any store that holds children's personal information.

title: No configuration that retains children's data indefinitely
